supplementaryReferences.title: South African trial harvest duration and native yields
supplementaryReferences.quote: seven to eight months after planting
supplementaryReferences.note: Pretoria Hillcrest rain-shelter trial, 2015/16 and 2016/17, drip irrigation on sandy clay loam. Commercial ginger Z. officinale at eight months: 38.3 t/ha fresh and 8.8 t/ha dry rhizomes in the well-watered treatment; African ginger was a different species with different values. No matched plant density is supplied, so no kg/plant or household drying conversion is derived. The abstract says open field, while Methods specifies rain shelter; conditions are retained.

supplementaryReferences.title: Confirmed culinary species and product
supplementaryReferences.doc: UF/IFAS: Ginger, Galangal, and Turmeric Production in Florida
supplementaryReferences.note: Extension identifies culinary ginger rhizomes used as spice, preserves and beverages. Florida planting and harvest months are not imported into the South African calendar.

supplementaryReferences.title: Harvest recommendation
supplementaryReferences.quote: seven to eight months after planting
supplementaryReferences.doc: University of Pretoria author manuscript: Gatabazi et al. (2022)
supplementaryReferences.note: The author abstract recommends harvest seven to eight months after planting; it is a rhizome crop-cycle duration, not a full-bearing tree age.

productionGuidance.products: fresh rhizomes; dried ginger recorded separately
care: Use the planting date to record the rhizome harvest cycle. The Pretoria trial reference is conditional, not a fixed calendar across climates.
Record fresh rhizome and dried spice weights separately; keep edible ginger distinct from ornamental or African ginger species.
purchase: Ask a local supplier for healthy, identified Zingiber officinale planting rhizomes; no South African cultivar-specific yield curve is verified.
